entities.summary:
Patrocles was a Macedonian general and writer who played a significant role in the Hellenistic period of Greece. He was born in unknown circumstances, but his writing on geographical subjects helped to shape our understanding of ancient Macedonia's geography.

Patrocles served as a commander under King Antigonus I Monophthalmus during the Wars of the Diadochi (322–311 BCE) and later became a prominent figure in the Ptolemaic Kingdom. His writings on geography were highly regarded by scholars, including the famous Greek geographer Strabo.

Patrocles' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his work influenced the development of cartography and geographic thought during the Renaissance. He is also remembered for his role in shaping the political landscape of Macedonia during a period of great turmoil.

In conclusion, Patrocles was a key figure in the ancient world whose contributions to geography, politics, and military strategy have left an enduring impact on our understanding of history.
